dialogue.text: When your father fought the dark lord, he had hoped to recruit a brave hero to lead and inspire the troops.
dialogue.speaker: Timble

dialogue.text: I've heard of him. Don't think I ever met him though.
dialogue.speaker: You

dialogue.text: I doubt you would have. I only met him after we lost the battle. He was the only man in the barracks.
dialogue.speaker: Timble

dialogue.text: I don't remember his name, but he stayed in town for a week.
dialogue.speaker: Timble

dialogue.text: Do you think he would have been strong enough to help?
dialogue.speaker: You

dialogue.text: Undoubtedly.
dialogue.speaker: Timble

dialogue.text: On his first day in the local tavern he told the townsfolk about his many great conquests. He only battles the strongest of foes, and scoffed at anyone who wasn't willing to take on the same challenges.
dialogue.speaker: Timble

dialogue.text: Is the demon king enough of a challange for him?
dialogue.speaker: You

dialogue.text: Yes, that's why he came to town. Unfortunately he was too late.
dialogue.speaker: Timble

dialogue.text: What was this hero like?
dialogue.speaker: You

dialogue.text: He was a very kind person. He spent his second day with the oddballs of the village. He never let them be alone.
dialogue.speaker: Timble

dialogue.text: That's very admirable.
dialogue.speaker: You

dialogue.text: Very, your majesty. He made a lot of friends that week.
dialogue.speaker: Timble

dialogue.text: And he's never come back to see them?
dialogue.speaker: You

dialogue.text: No, although perhaps he might someday.
dialogue.speaker: Timble

dialogue.text: We're on a roll Timble, I feel like nothing can stop us.
dialogue.speaker: You

dialogue.text: Careful, your majesty. We don't know what surprises this journey might hold.
dialogue.speaker: Timble

dialogue.text: What else was the hero up to, Timble?
dialogue.speaker: You

dialogue.text: Plenty, your majesty.
dialogue.speaker: Timble

dialogue.text: I got the sense that he was very reverent. On his fourth day, he assisted the townsfolk in burying the dead.
dialogue.speaker: Timble

dialogue.text: Were there many?
dialogue.speaker: You

dialogue.text: Many. Your fathers campaign had few survivors.
dialogue.speaker: Timble

dialogue.text: That night he visited each soldier's grave. He spent equal time at all except one. I was told that they had sacrificed themself to save several comrades. They were the first to fall in our final battle.
dialogue.speaker: Timble

dialogue.text: I hope our campaign doesn’t end like fathers.
dialogue.speaker: You

dialogue.text: You said he was in town for a week but have only told me of four days, what was the fifth like, Timble?
dialogue.speaker: You

dialogue.text: The fifth day we celebrated a festival in the local village. Some of the townspeople were playing games in the tavern that evening. He joined them, although I'm forgetting which games he played.
dialogue.speaker: Timble

dialogue.text: Huh... I guess these things are a reminder. He wouldn't touch games with any randomness or luck. Ended up just playing chess.
dialogue.speaker: Timble

dialogue.text: I'm not sure he fully understood the rules of the game. He spent every match obsessively defending all his pieces. No piece was unguarded.
dialogue.speaker: Timble

dialogue.text: Fascinating.

dialogue.text: We've come so far, Timble.
dialogue.speaker: You

dialogue.text: We have, your highness. Would you like me to tell you about the sixth day?
dialogue.speaker: Timble

dialogue.text: Please.
dialogue.speaker: You

dialogue.text: The sixth day was a strange one, since up until that point he had been very friendly with all the townsfolk.
dialogue.speaker: Timble

dialogue.text: Did someone do something to him?
dialogue.speaker: You

dialogue.text: The opposite, actually, sire. He picked a fight with one of the merchants. Accused him of hoarding money and underpaying his guard.
dialogue.speaker: Timble

dialogue.text: Was the merchant really doing all that?
dialogue.speaker: You

dialogue.text: I don't know. I haven't checked the merchant's balance sheets.
dialogue.speaker: Timble

dialogue.text: How are you feeling, sire? Are you ready for the final battle of our campaign?
dialogue.speaker: Timble

dialogue.text: Nervous, Timble. I guess I was hoping that hero you've been telling me about would have joined us by now.
dialogue.speaker: You

dialogue.text: The hero came too late to help your father. I suspect he'll always come too late to help you too.
dialogue.speaker: Timble

dialogue.text: So that's it? Just us and the army?
dialogue.speaker: You

dialogue.text: Yes, but perhaps we don't need him. On his last day, the hero visited me before he left.
dialogue.speaker: Timble

dialogue.text: Did he tell you anything important!?!?
dialogue.speaker: You

dialogue.text: He told me he had spoken with the demon king. That he could understand him. And then he told me we all need to be understood by someone.
dialogue.speaker: Timble

dialogue.text: That's what he said? It's...
dialogue.speaker: You

dialogue.text: Corny.
dialogue.speaker: You

dialogue.text: Yes sire, that's what he told me.
dialogue.speaker: Timble

dialogue.text: Huh...
dialogue.speaker: You

dialogue.text: Well, I guess we've come this far. Better start preparing for the battle.
dialogue.speaker: You
